answer.evidence: The garden bed is drawn as a flat plan view. The plank frame (rows 16-47) and the four soil ridges with dark furrows (rows 23-43) are all seen from directly above. The bottom plank (rows 45-47) is a thin frame strip with no front-edge line and no vertical south face. There is no front face of 3 or more rows, so no south-facing vertical surface is drawn. The bean plants are small decor details sitting on the soil. The kind is flat, and the drawing matches a top-down plate.

styleAnswer.evidence: The soil border carries speckle and mottling in several brown tones, and the bean rows add small green clusters with dark soil between them. Nothing reads as a flat fill, and near-flat coverage is 0%. Visible tones per tile are 5, above the reference grass (3) and below the paving (7), so density is comparable to the grass but a bit under the richer reference. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown and green rather than black, which fits dark_material_tone. The weak point is that the whole patch uses only 16 colours. That gives roughly 3-4 steps per material (soil, plank frame, bean foliage), against about 5-6 in Beodeul. The plank frame is thin and fairly flat, with little weathering or per-plank grain. The ground tiles do hold up against the references, so I pass it narrowly.
